h: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, י״א Motzei Yom Kippur, 11

p: Our Sages, of blessed memory, said
a heavenly voice goes forth and says:
and drink your wine with a good heart,
כִּי כְבָר רָצָה ה׳ אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ״.
for Hashem has already accepted your deeds."
And likewise on Motzei Shabbos Kodesh
such a heavenly voice goes forth,
what place is there for a Melaveh Malkah meal,
Do we not find in the Gemara
And I heard from my master and teacher, of blessed memory,
who said in the name of the Rav, the Gaon,
R. Y. Posner, of blessed memory,
one descends from a high roof
similar to what our Sages, of blessed memory, learned
from Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him
because he merited wisdom and holiness,
that comes from Hashem, may He be blessed,
into His holiness, may His Name be blessed, in completeness.
And likewise on Motzei Yom Kippur,
when our sins have been atoned
and we have become a new creation,
cleansed of all iniquity and transgression,
for we rejoice in this holiness.
And the meal of Motzei Shabbos
נִקְרֵאת סְעוּדַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
is called the meal of David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
because he "established the yoke of teshuvah"
a person can bring himself near
to His holiness, may His Name be blessed.
And likewise on Motzei Yom Kippur,
to His holiness, may His Name be blessed,
by way of forgiveness and atonement,
on Motzei Yom Kippur with joy.
Now, the verse uses the expressions
it would have been enough to write
to hint that we may drink wine;
so what need was there to write
And if it is to exclude what is stolen,
that is fitting as a warning about a mitzvah,
with which one does not fulfill one's obligation using stolen goods;
but in a person's ordinary eating,
as it is written, "Rejoice, young man, in your youth,
and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth"
and it is brought in the Gemara
"Up to here refers to words of Torah;
from here on, to good deeds:
God will bring you to judgment'" —
whether the good deeds were as they should be.
for it alludes to the Written Torah
For in the aspect of the Written Torah
as it is written, "The precepts of Hashem are upright,
And in the aspect of the Oral Torah
it is the cheering of the heart,
as it is written regarding Boaz,
And I heard from my master and teacher, of blessed memory,
that he said: for this reason
the Gemara says in several places
"according to the heart of this one,"
for the words of the Oral Torah
הֵם יוֹצְאִים מִקִּירוֹת לִבּוֹ שֶׁל הָאָדָם,
come out from the walls of a person's heart,
according to the holy feeling in his heart.
"For in much wisdom is much vexation"
the heart is straightened out of the "much vexation"
and drink of the wine I have mixed"
concerning what is written, "the wine I have mixed":
that the Holy One, blessed be He, pours in
the words of the Oral Torah,
And words of Torah are called
that is, because in all foods
is the words of Torah within them,
as is brought in the holy Zohar
that the sustenance of Torah scholars
than the food of the manna,
comes from the aspect of wisdom,
which "gives life to those who possess it" (Koheles 7:12),
that is, from the words of Torah
meaning that even the physical bread
that you eat on Motzei Yom Kippur
will have holy vitality in it
from the words of the Written Torah,
to which the notion of joy applies;
"and drink your wine with a good heart"
hints that in the physical wine
there will be the holy vitality
of the words of the Oral Torah,
which come from the "goodness of heart,"
due to the greatness of the holiness
that Yisrael attained on the holy day,
when they became a new creation,
pure of all sin and iniquity.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּכָל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ,
And likewise on every Motzei Shabbos Kodesh,
by virtue of the holiness of Shabbos.
